d_sv_content.name: Innovative Immunotherapy for Canine Lung Metastases: The CAALM Study
d_sv_content.tagline: Pioneering hope for dogs with metastatic cancer
d_sv_content.description: The CAALM Study is evaluating the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of a novel dog PDL1 antibody (UCD-PDL1). This cutting-edge trial seeks to optimize dosing while exploring the antibody’s potential to improve survival outcomes for dogs with oral melanoma that has spread to the lungs.
d_sv_content.requirements: Eligible Dogs:Weight: > 15 kg (33 lbs) and < 36 kg (79 lbs)Confirmed diagnosis of oral melanoma (via cytology or biopsy)Presence of one or more lung nodules consistent with metastatic diseaseExpected survival of > 4 weeksOther eligibility requirements will be assessed at the first visitCaregivers:Must be at least 18 years old, able to provide informed consent, and adhere to the study protocol.Time Commitment:Participation involves up to 6 biweekly treatments over a 98-day study period, including follow-up visits and monitoring.Adherence to Protocol:Owners must monitor their dog’s health, attend scheduled visits at UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine, and provide accurate updates through questionnaires and check-ins.
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Attend Scheduled Visits:Pre-enrollment screening (Days -7 to -1): Initial evaluation, including diagnostic imaging and bloodwork.Treatment visits (Days 0, 14, 28, 42, 56, and 70): Includes physical exams, blood sampling, thoracic radiographs, and antibody administration. Dogs will be required to spend the night at the hospital after the first antibody administration. Follow-up monitoring (Days 4, 7, and post-treatment): Includes physical exams, blood sampling and quality-of-life evaluations.Monitor Your Dog’s Health:Observe for any changes in behavior or health and report adverse events to the study team promptly.Adhere to Study Protocol:Ensure compliance with treatment schedules and follow any instructions provided by the study team.
d_sv_content.whoCan: Eligible Dogs:Weight: > 15 kg (33 lbs) and < 36 kg (79 lbs)Confirmed diagnosis of oral melanoma (via cytology or biopsy)Presence of one or more lung nodules consistent with metastatic diseaseExpected survival of > 4 weeksOther eligibility requirements will be assessed at the first visitEligible Owners:At least 18 years old and able to adhere to the study’s requirements, including appointments and questionnaires.Exclusion Criteria:Dogs are not eligible if they:Have received prior checkpoint inhibitor therapy.Have undergone recent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or corticosteroid treatment within two weeks of Day 0.Present with uncontrolled medical conditions that could interfere with treatment or data interpretation.
d_sv_content.benefits: Benefits:Access to cutting-edge immunotherapy at no cost, including diagnostics, imaging, and antibody treatments.Contribution to advancing cancer treatment for dogs through groundbreaking research.Risks:Possible side effects of the investigational antibody, such as infusion-related reactions or changes in laboratory test values.Stress associated with diagnostic tests, treatment, and clinic visits.
d_sv_content.compensation:
The study covers the cost of treatments, required diagnostics, and management of study-related adverse events (up to $2,000 per patient).

Owners are responsible for pre-enrollment screening costs, including initial consultations and eligibility diagnostics.

No monetary compensation is provided.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: Participation involves up to 6 biweekly treatments over a 98-day study period, including follow-up visits and monitoring.
